# Synthetic test data — expected outcomes

*Generated by `generate.py` — do not edit by hand. All people, e-mails, phones and addresses are fictitious.*

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `applications_2026_synthetic.csv` | 212 application rows, exact 2026 export format (UTF-8, `;`, CRLF), in posting order |
| `applications_2026_excel_mangled.csv` | Same rows after an Excel open+save: Windows-1252 (`?` for lost characters), birth dates `dd/mm/yyyy` → app must warn |
| `payments_2026_synthetic.csv` | 114 payment-form rows |
| `expected_applications.json` | Oracle per application: expected ID, import outcome, automatic flags, expected LLM verdicts |
| `expected_payments.json` | Oracle per payment row: which application ID it should match, and how |
| `config_2026_synthetic.json` | Season config (2026 courses/dates/fees; capacities invented) |
| `headers_2026.json` | Exact headers of the real 2026 exports |

## Summary

- Applications: 212 rows → 210 after removing 2 exact duplicates; 2 near-duplicates to review.
- Claiming Flemish status: 123.
- Automatic flags: CHOICE_GAP 2, DUPLICATE_CHOICE 1, NO_FIRST_CHOICE 2, OTHER_SESSION_COURSE 2, SHORT_MOTIVATION 2, TOO_OLD 1, YOUNG 24.
- IDs are assigned in true posting order (GMT offset taken into account), skipping exact duplicates.

Flag names used in the oracle: `OTHER_SESSION_COURSE`, `NO_FIRST_CHOICE`, `DUPLICATE_CHOICE`, `CHOICE_GAP`, `YOUNG`, `TOO_OLD`, `SHORT_MOTIVATION`. Base-population rows can also carry flags (e.g. random `>2` students) — `expected_applications.json` is authoritative.

## Deliberate edge cases — applications

| Case | Situation | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| E01 | Zoë Janssens: same form submitted 3× (3rd copy differs only in whitespace/case) | Keep the first; the other two are exact duplicates, removed automatically (no review needed). |
| E03 | Kateřina Procházka: resubmits next day with a corrected 2nd choice | Near-duplicate flag. Merge keeps the corrected choices AND the earliest timestamp. |
| E04 | Jolien Van den Broeck: resubmits 3 days later with a different e-mail and phone | Near-duplicate via name + birth date (e-mail differs). |
| E05 | Inès Girard: applies to BOTH sessions (two forms, 12 min apart) | NOT a duplicate. Two applications, two IDs, linked as the same person. Will pay twice. |
| E06 | Freja Jensen: Session I selected, but only Session II courses chosen | Flags OTHER_SESSION_COURSE + NO_FIRST_CHOICE. |
| E07 | Ellen Segers: Session II selected, but also a Session I course | Flag OTHER_SESSION_COURSE (student should submit a second form if they want both). |
| E08 | Arjun Raghunathan: only a 2nd choice, 1st empty | Flags NO_FIRST_CHOICE + CHOICE_GAP. |
| E09 | Febe De Wilde: same course as 1st and 2nd choice | Flag DUPLICATE_CHOICE. |
| E10 | Mehmet Çelik: 1st and 3rd choice, no 2nd | Flag CHOICE_GAP. |
| E11 | Wei Zhang: other session's columns all '(Not applying to Session II)' | Valid — no flag. |
| E12 | Lowie Van de Velde: years left '>2' (age 15) | Flag YOUNG (via years left). |
| E13 | Haruto Suzuki: age 14 at Session I start, says 2 years left | Flag YOUNG (via age). |
| E14 | Age boundary: Kato De Smet turns 15 on 20 July 2026 (Session I start); Lars Peeters turns 15 on 21 July 2026 | First: no flag (age 15). Second: flag YOUNG (age 14). |
| E15 | Lucía Martínez: born 2006 (age 20), mentions first bachelor year | Flag TOO_OLD. LLM motivation check should also flag 'university student'. |
| E16 | Hanne Jacobs: turns 19 on 4 Aug 2026 (day after Session II start) | No flag (age 18 on the start date). |
| E17 | Aoife Murphy: motivation of 25 words | Flag SHORT_MOTIVATION. |
| E18 | Word-count boundary: Seppe Van Acker 49 words; Lars Jacobs 50 words | 49 → SHORT_MOTIVATION; 50 → no flag (threshold: fewer than 50). |
| E19 | Wout Smets: motivation contains their name (also in CAPITALS), school and e-mail | Redaction test: all four must be replaced by placeholders before the text goes to the LLM. |
| E20 | Kato Van den Broeck: motivation in Dutch | No automatic flag; LLM: no flag. |
| E21 | Ananya Iyer: long enough, but says they aren't interested in science | No automatic flag; LLM motivation check should flag it. |
| E22 | Pieter Van den Broeck: motivation with double quotes, semicolons and line breaks | CSV parsing: must stay one field; no flag. |
| E23 | Freja Østergaard: claims Flemish status, school 'International School of Brussels' | Goes to the school check; LLM: not Flemish → human confirms non-FL (fee 430/330/250). |
| E24 | Lowie Van Damme: Flemish, school written 'St Vincent Ieper' | LLM: Flemish (alias of Sint-Vincentiuscollege Ieper); store alias. |
| E25 | Matthias Smets: claims Flemish, school 'Athénée Royal d'Uccle 1' (French-speaking) | LLM: not Flemish → plain non-FL, no special status. |
| E26 | Jasper Vermeulen: Dutch-language school in Brussels | LLM: Flemish (Brussels Dutch-language schools count). |
| E27 | Kato Van Damme: school given as 'middelbare school' | LLM: unclear → human decides. |
| E28 | Many names with non-Western characters (ş, ț, ł, ø, ễ, Ó…) | Must survive import/export unchanged. The Excel-mangled file must trigger the 're-saved in Excel' warning. |
| E29 | Joren Pauwels: 'send all organizational e-mails also to parent' not ticked | Parent still gets admission/payment e-mails; not other organizational mails. |
| E30 | Accommodation fallbacks: Hélène Coppens (FULL → don't come), Seppe Bogaerts (FULL → EVENING), Joren Wouters (DAY, N/A) | Used by the dorm-full handling in phase 2. |
| E31 | Lien Goossens: name typed in CAPITALS with extra spaces | Normalise for matching/display (trim; keep original in RawImports). |
| E32 | Two applications 2 minutes apart across the DST switch (GMT+1 → GMT+2) | Ordering must use the GMT offset; the 01:59 GMT+1 one is first. |
| E33 | Lore Peeters: student e-mail = parent e-mail | No flag; mail merge must not send the same e-mail twice. |

## Deliberate edge cases — payments

| Case | Situation |
|---|---|
| P03 | e-mail matches the student e-mail after trimming + lower-casing (e.g. `Mads Jensen`, expected SOS26-0129) |
| P04 | unknown e-mail, exact student name (e.g. `Ciarán O'Brien`, expected SOS26-0070) |
| P05 | unknown e-mail, name without accents (e.g. `Kato Van Acker`, expected SOS26-0185) |
| P06 | unknown e-mail, surname first (e.g. `De Backer Nina`, expected SOS26-0003) |
| P07 | unknown e-mail, PARENT's name given → also match against parent names (e.g. `Elena Ó Súilleabháin`, expected SOS26-0143) |
| P08 | unknown e-mail, surname typo → top-3 candidates for a human (e.g. `Ilse Smet`, expected SOS26-0030) |
| P09 | Payer matches nobody (`Jean Dupont`) → manual |
| P10 | Student with two applications (E05) pays twice with the same e-mail → session ambiguous, human links each payment |
| P12 | The very same payment-form submission twice (identical row) → exact duplicate |
| — | Many proof files share names like `screenshot.png` / `image.png` → file-name matching alone is not unique |

Most other payments match on the student e-mail (plain) or the parent e-mail.

## Not covered by synthetic data

- Real quoting/BOM details of the website export (see DESIGN.md §8 unverified assumptions).
- Proof-of-payment images (phase 3: create a handful of fake bank screenshots then).
